maximum detected UCMR 3 PFOA or PFOS result at the same water system where the result sign is the equals code; when the system has only non-detect prior rows, the maximum reported MRL is used as the sourced censoring bound; missing only when the system has no UCMR 3 PFOA or PFOS row

row_selection.rule: Keep entry-point samples with a documented PFOA or PFOS result sign and a nonmissing CollectionDate; select the earliest sample per water system by CollectionDate, breaking ties by SampleID; apply the fixed half-open date windows that embargo December 2023 and December 2024; count and report any first-sample rows excluded by the windows.

limitations: UCMR 5 is occurrence monitoring at entry points, not compliance monitoring; a result at or above the minimum reporting level is not a violation or an MCL determination.
The label is sample-level at one entry point; systems with multiple facilities or sample points can have heterogeneous PFOA or PFOS results.

The final UCMR 5 dataset was released in 2026; system size reflects a 2021 vintage, UCMR 3 files were revised, and self-reported additional data elements may have been edited after sampling. This is current-vintage retrospective research, not proof of historical operational availability.
Results below the UCMR 5 minimum reporting level are censored, so the label captures detection at the reporting threshold, not concentration magnitude.

First-sample collection dates follow monitoring schedules rather than random assignment, so chronological splits can reflect rollout differences by system size, state, and laboratory capacity. First samples whose dates fall in the December embargo or outside 2023-2026 are excluded by the fixed split policy and are counted in a source check.

UCMR 5 covered community water systems and non-transient non-community water systems, not transient non-community systems, and small-system participation was a representative sample rather than a census.

Additional data element concepts are stored as rows in the AdditionalDataElement field rather than as header columns; the builder filters the documented values, aggregates Response values by system and sample keys, and fails if any declared feature has zero coverage.

For UCMR 3 systems with only non-detect PFOA or PFOS rows, the prior maximum uses the maximum reported MRL as a sourced censoring bound, not an observed concentration and not zero. The prior maximum is missing only when the system has no UCMR 3 PFOA or PFOS row.
The occurrence text file carries a non-UTF-8 micro sign byte in the concentration unit text; the builder decodes publisher text with the Windows-1252 codec and checks UCMR 5 and UCMR 3 units.
This is a predictive association task, not a causal analysis of source-water contamination or treatment effectiveness.

selection.conditioning: No selection on the binary target; all eligible entry-point samples inside the fixed windows are retained after the earliest-first-sample rule, and out-of-window first samples are counted rather than relabeled or silently dropped.
selection.evidence: The earliest entry-point sample per water system is selected by CollectionDate with SampleID tie-break; the current sample AnalyticalResultsSign and AnalyticalResultValue are used only for the label and are excluded from features.

vintage.evidence: Final UCMR 5 occurrence dataset released August 2026; historical operational availability of features is not proven.

external_threshold.source: UCMR 5 minimum reporting level for PFOA and PFOS, fixed before sampling

task.decision_user: State drinking-water program manager or utility planning lead deciding which systems to prioritize for PFAS technical assistance, confirmatory sampling, and treatment planning before the first UCMR 5 laboratory results are available.
task.outcome_horizon: Laboratory analysis and reporting of the first sample; the label is observed in the final UCMR 5 dataset released in August 2026.
task.population: Public water systems subject to UCMR 5 with at least one entry-point sample (SamplePointType of EP) and a PFOA or PFOS analytical result carrying a documented result sign. One row per water system: the earliest sample by CollectionDate with a deterministic tie-break by SampleID. Samples with missing CollectionDate, non-entry-point sample types, or no documented PFOA or PFOS result sign are excluded. First samples whose dates fall in the December embargo or outside 2023-2026 are excluded from the shipped splits and counted.
task.prediction_time: Immediately before the first UCMR 5 entry-point sample is collected, recorded as CollectionDate; all inputs predate that sample result.
task.question: Will a public water system first UCMR 5 entry-point sample contain PFOA or PFOS at or above the UCMR 5 minimum reporting level?
task.usefulness: The first sample result is unknown until laboratory analysis; the model ranks systems by pre-sample contamination risk using prior UCMR 3 results, system size and source type, prior PFAS testing and treatment, and reported potential sources. Current-sample result fields are excluded from inputs.

construction_notes:
Prior failure corrected at the source semantics. The additional data element file is long-format: PWSID, FacilityID, SamplePointID, SampleEventCode, AdditionalDataElement, Response, IfOtherText. The five declared concepts are values of AdditionalDataElement, not header columns. The builder now filters PFASOccurrence, PFASTreatment, PotentialPFASSources, PotentialPFASSourcesDetail, and TreatmentInformation, aggregates nonempty Response codes by event, then by sample point, then by system, and fails with the selected member, header, data element values, and coverage if any declared feature has zero nonempty coverage. The two checks that previously passed literal True now compute outcomes from rows: the label check compares the emitted positive count with an independent sign-and-value recomputation, and the additional-data check uses actual mapped values and nonempty response counts.

Prior UCMR 3 maximum corrected. For detected rows the maximum uses the reported numeric result. For systems with only non-detect rows, the maximum uses the maximum reported UCMR 3 MRL as a sourced censoring bound, not zero and not an invented value. The prior detection flag is 0 for monitored systems with no detected result, 1 for at least one detected result, and missing when the system has no UCMR 3 PFOA or PFOS row. UCMR 3 MRL and unit fields are now read and checked.

The population rule remains the earliest entry-point PFOA or PFOS sample per water system by CollectionDate with SampleID tie-break. The fixed half-open windows and December embargos are unchanged. The builder now records the selected, shipped, and excluded counts and the excluded date span in a source check instead of silently losing first samples outside the windows. The prior review observed 234 such rows; this build reports the actual count.
Text decoding remains Windows-1252 with replacement so the micro sign byte in concentration units decodes without a Unicode failure. UCMR 5 and UCMR 3 unit checks are computed from included rows. Size and water-type code checks are evaluated on shipped rows only, so unrelated codes elsewhere in the download cannot fail the build. All failure messages are bounded to 4000 characters and carry the selected archive member, observed header, and missing names where relevant.

Honest gaps: this write-only phase did not re-download or re-read the live archives, so archive member names and the additional data element values are resolved at runtime and any mismatch fails with observed evidence. There is no publication-date or full-row availability ledger, so timing observations remain empty, training label timing stays unverified, and historical feature availability before each sample is assumed rather than proven. The current UCMR 5 snapshot is retrospective research, not a historical forecasting claim. No metrics, training, qualification, or packaging are performed.
